name: Freenove 4WD Smart Car Kit
description: A Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040) microcontroller car — the cheapest and least capable of Freenove's three overlapping 4WD car families, not to be confused with Freenove's own Raspberry Pi SBC or Arduino siblings of nearly the same name. No camera, no vision processing, and it's programmed in Arduino C++ rather than MicroPython despite the Pico branding.

sourcing: Specs compiled from Freenove's own store listing and documentation site for FNK0089 as of this build. Independent Amazon review data and the LED matrix's exact pixel count on this specific unit were not directly verifiable — confirm before purchase.

pricing.summary: FNK0089 lists at $44.99 with no compute board, $49.99 with a Raspberry Pi Pico included, or $54.99 with a Pico W (needed for any WiFi/app control) — direct from Freenove's own store, with matching Amazon listings for each configuration. That makes it the cheapest kit in this subcategory, well under ELEGOO's $75.99 Arduino-class car and SunFounder PiCar-X's ~$89.99.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Freenove's GitHub repository for this kit is real, browsable source, but it's licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 — a Creative Commons license whose non-commercial clause is not OSI-approved as open source, so no Open Source badge applies here despite the code being public. The pan-tilt LED-matrix panel in this product's photo also reads visually wider than the single 8×8 module Freenove's own documentation describes for this SKU, a spec discrepancy worth confirming against your specific unit.
